weakness: The pipeline sent each arm straight to the key centre in its home gripper yaw and pressed with move_to calls that had no avoid list. An 18 cm post 1.5 cm beside the left key overlapped the 16 cm wide gripper palm: the planner (whose model does not include the gripper) still returned success, the palm jammed on the post 5 cm above the hover pose, the key never fired and the bowl could not be driven left (7 of 10 seeds lost).
how_found: Questioned A13 (free path to the key). The pipeline treated a key as a point and the gripper as having no size; real buttons sit among clutter, and the API planner only avoids what it is given (and, it turned out, not with the gripper's own geometry).
why_missed: The empty table made every straight top-down approach succeed, and move_to returning True looked like proof that the gripper got there. I never compared the reached pose with the target, and never asked how wide the tool is relative to the free space around the target.
fix: Measure the static obstacles once (get_obstacles minus the task objects) and pass them as avoid; model the gripper as a 16x9 cm footprint reaching 17 cm below the flange; choose the gripper yaw (0 or 90 deg) and press-point offset within the key's capture radius that clears every obstacle box by 1.5 cm over the whole press stroke; approach from above the tallest nearby obstacle, then descend; accept a move only if the measured pose is within 1.2 cm of the target.
general_rule: Before approaching a target, check the tool's full footprint (not just its tip) against known obstacles over the whole approach and stroke, choose an orientation or offset that clears them, and verify the reached pose instead of trusting the planner's success flag.

weakness: The pipeline never checked that the receptacle was empty. With a canister standing in the bowl it servoed the bowl under the ball, the ball bounced off the canister, and 9 of 10 seeds failed. A thinner stick (v3, rejected) slid aside or was flung out by the bowl's starts and stops, which hid the problem half the time.
how_found: Listed what the pipeline assumes about the goal region rather than about the moving objects: nothing in the code reads the bowl's contents, and on a real robot a container often still holds the last item.
why_missed: The task statement only talks about moving the bowl and catching the ball; I modelled the bowl as a target point, not as a container whose state is a precondition.
fix: Tried: before anything else, list objects whose box sits inside the bowl; take each out with a horizontal side grasp from the robot side just above the rim (a top-down grasp would hit the shelves overhead), lift 7.5 cm, back out, set it down standing between the keys, open, and pull the fingers away before any later close. Pushing it over the far rim failed (the palm rode up on the rim). The clearing works (0.4 overall), but it costs ~8 s plus 2.4 s of gripper closing with one blocking primitive at a time, and on 5 seeds the ball lands within 5.7-11.7 s, so 0.8 was out of reach. Marked unsolved after 4 repair iterations and reverted the pipeline to round 1 (attempt kept in attempts/pipeline_v4_unsolved.py).
general_rule: Check that the goal location or receptacle is actually free before relying on it, and when it must be cleared first, budget the clearing time against the deadline at the start instead of discovering the overrun afterwards.

weakness: Round 1 made the press configuration obstacle-aware but from a single snapshot taken at the start. A post that slid in next to the left key at 4-6 s (after the arms were in place) jammed the hovering gripper exactly as in v2, and the left key stopped working for the rest of the episode. (The same post arriving at 7-9 s, v6, only cost half the seeds; a block lying on the key, v5, was simply shoved off by the press.)
how_found: Read the round-1 fix as a new assumption: 'obstacles are static, measure them once'. Real workspaces change while the robot works, and nothing in the loop re-perceived them.
why_missed: The fix for round 1 was written against a static obstacle, so it inherited the original program's habit of perceiving the scene once and then acting open-loop on that snapshot, even though the main control loop already re-perceives the ball and the bowl 50 times a second.
fix: Tried: re-read the obstacles every 0.2 s (one noisy reading, re-snapshot averaged over five readings if anything moved more than 3 cm), re-plan the press configuration only when the current one no longer clears (hysteresis against sensor noise), plan against where a moving obstacle will be 0.3-1.5 s later, and use a double margin on re-plans so one re-plan suffices. It works (the arm turns away from the arriving post and presses again), but each re-plan costs 1-1.6 s of key downtime (lift, turn, descend) inside the 5-8 s window in which several seeds land; v7 stayed at 0.5-0.7 over six iterations on a noisy shared host, so it is marked unsolved and the pipeline is reverted to round 1 (attempt in attempts/pipeline_v7_unsolved.py).
general_rule: Treat every perceived fact the plan depends on, including obstacles and free space, as something that can change: re-check it inside the control loop and re-plan when it no longer holds, rather than snapshotting it once at the start.
